subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps by repairing renderer/anchor behavior first, by adding a TUI auto-scroll preference, or by waiting for stronger live repro/upstream dependency proof?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the right fix crosses terminal UX policy, dependency ownership, and possible new settings surface rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Repair Renderer And Anchor Behavior
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then preserve follow-to-tail behavior only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add TUI Auto-Scroll Preference
options.body: Expose explicit terminal auto-scroll control if maintainers want user choice, accepting the additional config/settings and upgrade-proof burden.

options.title: Hold For Live Repro Or Upstream
options.body: Keep the issue open until a current-main PTY capture or upstream pi-tui decision proves the exact failure and repair boundary.

recommendation.title: Repair Renderer And Anchor Behavior
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then preserve follow-to-tail behavior only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on TUI state and event-handler behavior around the implicated streaming path.
